ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows two rays starting from point S that are perpendicular to each other, forming a right angle; one original ray can be regarded as direction 0°, and the other as direction 90°. According to the method, represent each new ray as a direction angle between 0° and 90°, and the angle formed by any two rays is the difference of these direction angles. The goal is to use as few new direction angles as possible so that the pairwise differences include 10°, 20°, 30°, 40°, 50°, 60°, 70°, 80°. First prove the lower bound: if only 2 new rays are added, then there are a total of 4 rays, and there are at most C(4,2)=6 pairs of rays forming angles; among them, the original two rays already give 90°, so at most only 5 pairs remain that can provide non-right angles, making it impossible to cover the required 8 angles. Therefore at least 3 must be added. Then give a construction: add three rays with direction angles 10°, 40°, 70°. At this time the set of direction angles is {0°,10°,40°,70°,90°}, and the pairwise differences include 10°, 20°, 30°, 40°, 50°, 60°, 70°, 80°: for example, 10-0=10, 90-70=20, 40-10=30, 40-0=40, 90-40=50, 70-10=60, 70-0=70, 90-10=80. Therefore 3 rays can do it, and fewer than 3 rays are impossible, so the minimum number is 3.

method.method_draft: Model every ray by its direction angle from one side of the right angle, with the two original rays at 0° and 90°. The task becomes choosing as few additional numbers in (0,90) as possible so that the set of pairwise differences contains 10°, 20°, ..., 80°. For a lower bound, if only 2 new rays were added, there would be 4 total rays and only 6 pairs of rays, one of which gives the original 90° angle, leaving at most 5 pairs to realize the 8 required non-right angles; impossible. For an upper bound, add rays at 10°, 40°, and 70°. Then the pairwise differences among {0,10,40,70,90} include 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, and 80 degrees. Therefore the minimum is 3.
